🔥🇲🇽 <u>RUFFO GOES HOME, AND SHEINBAUM WANTS ANSWERS</u>

Former PAN governor Ernesto Ruffo Appel, on trial in the multibillion-peso huachicol fiscal case, left the Altiplano prison for house arrest in Ensenada. He went by road: roughly 2,800 km and about 41 hours. Sheinbaum raised it at this morning's Security Cabinet and asked the FGR to explain the route: "The judge's order was followed, but I don't have certainty that it was that way." The FGR says the case against him hasn't changed.
banner: RUFFO: 41-HOUR ROAD TRIP TO HOUSE ARREST

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "First of all, it's the first time Azteca raises its hand." "If the prosecutor's office has evidence of any illegality against anyone, it has to open an investigation, but not because TV Azteca says so, but because there is evidence that actually links them to a crime. It is not a media outlet's say-so." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera A TV Azteca reporter asked about her own network's report that Amílcar Olán is in Switzerland and has alleged ties to Morena figures, including Andy López Beltrán. Asked whether she would call on the Attorney General's Office to act: "No. The prosecutor's office should act as it should always act." TV Azteca is owned by Ricardo Salinas Pliego.

🇲🇽⚖️ "Freedoms, but not freedom as the right or the conservatives see it, which is the freedom of the market." "That is the one they defend. It is not a regime of freedoms, because they are neither in favor of the right to protest nor do they agree with the right to free expression, because if they did, they would have upheld it when they governed. The objective is to guarantee the people of Mexico well-being, freedoms, democracy. But democracy not seen as the democracy of an elite, but the representation of the people, and social justice, which is the dream of Morelos and of Hidalgo." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera She said the core constitutional changes of the Fourth Transformation will be very hard to reverse: the universal senior pension and the rule that the minimum wage must rise above inflation are now in the Constitution. Morelos was born September 30, 1765.

🇲🇽✊ "Working fewer hours does not mean working less." "After more than a century with a 48-hour workweek, Mexico now has a route to advance toward 40 hours in 2030. This reduction will be carried out without reducing wages, without reducing benefits, because working fewer hours does not mean working less; it means advancing toward a better balance between work, family life and personal life." — Marath Bolaños, Secretary of Labor, Mañanera The first 2-hour cut starts next year, then 2 hours a year until 2030. More than 13 million workers benefit directly. With the 40-hour week, overtime starts at hour 41 instead of hour 49, and triple-pay hours start at hour 53 instead of 57. The share of workers doing more than 48 hours already fell from 27.1% to 22.2% between 2020 and 2025.

🇲🇽✊ In 2018 the minimum wage didn't buy one basic food basket. Today it buys almost two. "In 2018 the minimum wage bought approximately 0.8 basic baskets. I repeat, 0.8 basic baskets. That is, it wasn't even enough to buy one basic basket. Today it allows buying 1.9 basic baskets, practically two, more than double what it did in 2018." — Marath Bolaños, Secretary of Labor, Mañanera The daily minimum wage went from 88 pesos in 2018 to 315 in 2026, a 154% real increase, or 9,584 pesos a month. INEGI's employment survey counted 60.7 million people employed in August, 1.3 million more than in August 2025 and the highest figure for any August. The rule that the minimum wage must rise above inflation is now in the Constitution.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's Exports Jump 40.4% in August</u>

INEGI data via El Economista: Mexico exported $78.01 billion in August, 40.4% more than a year earlier, and returned to a $605.4 million trade surplus. Electrical and electronic equipment exports rose 122.3%. From January to August, Mexico ran a $9.86 billion surplus, against a $913 million deficit in the same months of 2025.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Minimum Wage Now Buys 1.9 Food Baskets, Up From 0.8 in 2018</u>

Labor Secretary Marath Bolaños presented the "Labor Spring" numbers. The minimum wage rose from 88 pesos a day in 2018 to 315 in 2026, a 154% real recovery. In 2018 it bought 0.8 basic food baskets; today it buys 1.9. The share of people working more than 48 hours a week fell from 27.1% in 2020 to 22.2% in 2025, and the road to a 40-hour week starts with 46 hours in 2027.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Oaxaca: Mixtec Community Defender Shot Dead</u>

Humberto García Cruz was a community defender in Santa Cruz Itundujia, Oaxaca, and a member of Sembrando Vida. On September 21 he was shot several times as he and his wife returned from their plot. She survived by throwing herself to the ground. He accompanied neighbors whose rights had been violated as they sought help from the authorities. Cedhapi is demanding that the Oaxaca State Prosecutor's Office find those responsible and protect his family.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Religious Right: From the Cristeros to the PAN</u>

In Contralínea, Pablo Moctezuma Barragán traces the line: the Sinarquistas, Los Tecos, MURO, El Yunque, and the PAN cadres they fed, a link that went public under Fox and Calderón. In 2008, PAN Jalisco governor Emilio González Márquez pledged 90 million pesos of public money to a Cristero martyrs' shrine. The first 30 million had to be returned after protests. It's the same "God, Country and Family" script used by Milei, Kast and Trump, and it's aimed straight at the Reform Laws.

text:
🇲🇽📜 <u>Sheinbaum: Undoing the 4T's Rights Takes Two-Thirds of Congress</u>

Sheinbaum says rolling back the social rights written into Mexico's Constitution over eight years of 4T government would be "very complex" in the short term: any force that tries would need a two-thirds majority. She called the current legislature the "Constituent Congress of the Fourth Transformation." It brought Pemex and CFE back as public companies, recognized Indigenous peoples, and made welfare programs constitutional rights.
